comments.content: `retryConnect` runs on a background goroutine and writes `c.connManager`, `c.streamManager` and `c.subManager` (and `Close`/`Health`/`checkClient`/`Publish`/`Subscribe` read them) without any synchronization, so once the client is in the retry state every publish/subscribe/health call races with these assignments (`go test -race` will flag it). There is also a partial-initialization window: `c.connManager` is published before `streamManager`/`subManager` are set, so a concurrent `CreateTopic`/`CreateStream` can pass `checkClient` and then dereference a still-nil `c.streamManager` (panic). Guard these fields with a mutex (or an atomic pointer) and assign the connected manager last.
comments.suggestion_code:
c.mu.Lock()
		c.streamManager = newStreamManager(js, c.logger)
		c.subManager = newSubscriptionManager(batchSize)
		c.connManager = connManager // publish last: readers must never see a connected manager without the managers above
		c.mu.Unlock()

comments.content: The retry goroutine has no cancellation and is not coordinated with `Close()`. If the app shuts down (or the process closes the datasource) while retrying, `retryConnect` keeps looping and can establish a connection after `Close` has run; that connection is then never closed (goroutine + connection leak, reconnect-after-shutdown). It also has no single-flight guard: `PubSubWrapper.Connect()` re-invokes `Client.Connect()` on health-down, so every failed attempt spawns yet another eternal loop and, eventually, another live connection. Add a stop channel/context cancelled from `Close` (and checked before/inside the loop) and ensure only one retry loop can run at a time.
comments.suggestion_code: c.startRetry() // single-flight; loop selects on c.done / ctx.Done()

comments.content: This branch cannot be reached in practice: `ConnectionManager.Connect()` already creates JetStream and only assigns `cm.jStream` on success, so the getter returns `errJetStreamNotConfigured` only if `Connect()` failed — which is handled by the branch above. If it ever did trigger, the just-opened connection is leaked (no `connManager.Close()`) while the next iteration creates a new manager. Prefer closing the manager before retrying and dropping the dead branch.

comments.content: The retry loop is unbounded, uses a fixed interval with no backoff/jitter, and logs every failure at Error level. Terminal failures (bad creds file, auth/TLS rejection, invalid server) will therefore log forever and spin a goroutine indefinitely. Also, the initial failure is reported twice (Errorf here and again in this first iteration, while `ConnectionManager.Connect` logs it at Debug), and `Connect()` now returns an error *and* starts a retry, so callers cannot tell whether the failure is fatal or will be retried. Consider backoff with a cap, and a clear contract (either return the error and let the caller retry, or retry internally and return nil).

comments.content: `nats.DefaultTimeout` is the client connect timeout (~2s), not a retry interval. Binding the retry cadence to a third-party constant silently shortens every existing wait that uses it (previously 10s), so the not-connected paths in `Subscribe` now sleep only ~2s and the retry loop hammers the server every 2s; the value also changes if the nats library changes it. Keep an explicit package constant for the retry interval.
